Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/24059

Merged duplicate: issues 24059 (DysruptionHub, Maple Plain) and 24200 (NPR roundup entry for the Maple Plain Water System) are the same incident; one record closes both.
Part of the coordinated July 26-28, 2026 attacks on internet-exposed operational technology at US water and wastewater systems (30+ systems in Minnesota plus Georgia, Michigan, New Jersey and other states; the FBI says at least seven states). CISA's July 30 alert and its July 2026 update describe Iranian-affiliated actors targeting internet-facing PLCs (Rockwell, Schneider, Siemens), changing passwords and IP addresses to lock operators out and, for the first time, stealing PLC project files. No federal or state attribution has been made; experts suspect Iran's IRGC (pattern consistent with CyberAv3ngers per Tenable), so the actor is coded external Unknown with motive Unknown, and the suspicion is only noted. Method at this specific utility is not public, so hacking variety and vector are Unknown (the campaign generally used internet-exposed devices with default or weak credentials). Template Hacking-ext-unknown used for actor/action only; no data theft was reported, so no confidentiality block, and the asset is the control system with role OT rather than a web application. Consider linking all the July 2026 water records with one campaign_id.
Impact: automated controls were affected and staff ran the system manually; service was not interrupted for customers. Availability Interruption is coded for the loss of automated control, integrity Unknown because the city has not said what was changed. A reviewer may drop Interruption since customer service continued.
Discovery: city employees identified the incident early on July 27 -> internal, method Unknown.
Victim: City of Maple Plain, Hennepin County (population about 1,800). NAICS 221310 (issue said 2213). Government Local. Employee count 11 to 100 is an estimate for a small city.

event_chain.summary: Access to water utility controls (method not disclosed)

summary: On Monday, July 27, 2026 a cybersecurity incident affected automated controls supporting the water utility of Maple Plain, Minnesota. City staff identified it early that morning and switched to manual contingency procedures, so drinking water stayed safe and water and wastewater service continued; the city declared a local state of emergency (July 26-28) and the council held an emergency meeting. Maple Plain was one of more than 30 Minnesota water systems hit in a coordinated attack on internet-exposed operational technology that also struck Braham, Plymouth and South St. Paul and utilities in other states.
